newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-U.S. aids the Australia 10-yr bond rebound.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-U.S. aids the Australia 10-yr bond rebound.

text.p: *The Australian 10-year bond futures contract extended Wednesday's rebound during SYCOM to a fresh 3-1/2 year high of 93.430 aided by a strong rally in U.S. Treasuries.
*U.S. 30-year bond yield dives through psychological 6.50 percent barrier after the June CPI rose a mere 0.1 percent.
The September Australian 10-year bond futures contract extended Wednesday's rebound during SYCOM, striking a fresh 3-1/2 year high of 93.430 at one stage, aided by a strong rally in U.S. Treasuries.
The contract ended afterhours trade at 93.420, up smartly from Wednesday's 93.345 dayside finish and holding above the market's previous peak of 94.415 set last Thursday.

A local currency-led sell-off on Wednesday saw the 10-year bond revisit support at 93.235, but the move once again proved a solid base and triggered a short squeeze going into the pit close, traders said.

The rebound has seen the contract scramble back above a rising trendline which has been running since late June from 92.825, and it remains well clear of a broader trendline from 91.700 at the beginning of April.

U.S. Treasuries rallied after its June CPI rose a mere 0.1 percent to an annual rate of 2.3 percent and saw the U.S. 30-year bond yield dive through the psychological 6.50 percent barrier to its lowest level since December last year.
Australia releases its own CPI next week and a recent Reuters poll of economists showed expectations centring on a flat outcome for an annual rate of just 0.6 percent.

Such an outcome, along with a forecast 0.6 percent rise in underlying inflation to year-on-year growth of 1.7 percent, is expected to see a further contraction in the Australian/U.S. 10-year yield differential.
This spread is currently retesting 40 basis points, having briefly dipped to around 35 b.p. last week, and where a clear break brings major support at 25 b.p. into view, analysts said.
